children: Milky Mist Dairy Food shares hit the upper circuit limit in Tuesday's trading session after the company reported a more than 1,000 percent jump in standalone net profit for the quarter ended June 30, 2026.
Shares of the company quoted at Rs 232.03 per share on the NSE, up 10 percent. Its market capitalisation stood at Rs 17,862.68 crore.
The company reported a more than 1,000 percent rise in standalone net profit at Rs 64.5 crore for the quarter ended June 30, 2026, compared with Rs 5.7 crore in the year-ago period.
The recently listed company's revenue rose 45 percent to Rs 973 crore in the quarter, from Rs 673 crore in the year-ago period.
Balaji Rao Mudili, Research Analyst at Bonanza, said most Indian dairy companies buy milk from farmers and sell much of it as packaged liquid milk, which is a low-margin commodity.

Milky Mist, however, avoids liquid milk and converts the milk it procures into products such as paneer, cheese, curd, butter, ghee, yoghurt, ice cream and UHT long-shelf-life items, sold under the Milky Mist brand. The company has also expanded into ready-to-cook and ready-to-eat foods, he said.

Mudili said the company's focus on value-added and higher-margin products has helped improve its overall margin mix. However, having only one facility in Tamil Nadu indicates a high concentration, he added.

Paneer, cheese and curd together accounted for 52.3 percent of the company's revenue in the first quarter of FY27. On an annual basis, the three products accounted for 59.05 percent of FY26 revenue, down from 66.16 percent in FY24, indicating gradual diversification in the product mix.

According to Mudili, Milky Mist's paneer and curd typically sell at prices 10-30 percent above those of large Indian brands. Its gross margin stood at 34.21 percent in Q1FY27, compared with 26-30 percent for Hatsun, Heritage and Dodla.

The management has also attributed the performance of ice cream, curd and yoghurt to an extended summer season, particularly in southern India. Ice cream sales increased 60 percent year-on-year, while yoghurt sales rose 153 percent.

Arpit Jain, Joint MD, Arihant Capital Markets, however, noted that while Milky Mist profit jumped 1000% in Q1FY2027 quarter but it needs base-effect caveat. Q1FY26 was an exceptionally weak quarter for the company.

The company has been clocking 31 percent revenue CAGR and consistently accelerating PAT growth each year since FY24. This trend suggests that the growth is genuine and the company’s business is improving. It is not simply a one-quarter fluke. Now the debt-paydown benefit from IPO proceeds hasn't even hit the P&L yet, which is a real forward tailwind, he said.

"Against FY26 PAT of Rs 127 crore, the company’s P/E stands at 130x. Even annualizing the strong Q1 numbers (Rs 64.68cr × 4 ≈ Rs 259cr), forward P/E is still 68x, expensive even against Hatsun (60-71x), and multiples of Dodla/Heritage/Parag (20-31x)," he added.

If you look closely, at 130x trailing / 68x forward earnings, the market has already priced-in years of continued 30%+ growth and margin expansion. The valuation is also well above what any comparable Indian dairy or FMCG name trades at. Overall the company’s fundamentals look strong, it is maintaining its leadership position in packaged paneer market and is expanding into new geographies like Maharashtra, which looks promising. However, just one quarter results should not be a reason to jump into buying the company. Valuation are steep and one needs to be careful before entering, he further added.
Shares of the company have risen 28 percent since their listing on August 18.
The shares had listed at Rs 165 on both the BSE and NSE, registering a premium of 17.85 percent over the issue price.
